model_annotation:
This plot illustrates trade data over time, showing exports, imports, and the trade balance (Saldo) in billions of US dollars (Mrd. US-Dollar). The x-axis represents time on a linear scale, spanning from 2020 to late 2023, with major tick labels at 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and a second 2023 marking toward the right. The left y-axis corresponds to exports and imports, ranging from 0 to 400 billion US dollars with tick intervals of 50. The right y-axis corresponds to the trade balance (Saldo), ranging from approximately -200 to 400 with tick intervals of 100.

The blue solid line represents imports (Importe, left scale), which starts at approximately 200 billion US dollars in early 2020, dips to roughly 170 in mid-2020, then rises steadily through 2021, reaching around 240 by late 2021. It continues climbing to a peak of approximately 290 in mid-2022, then fluctuates between roughly 260 and 280 through 2023, before rising sharply at the end of the series to approximately 345. The purple/mauve solid line represents exports (Exporte, left scale), starting near 130 billion US dollars in early 2020, dipping slightly in mid-2020, then gradually increasing through 2021 and 2022 to approximately 180 by mid-2022, after which it remains relatively stable between 165 and 180, ending near 185 at the end of the series. The light blue vertical bars represent the trade balance (Saldo, right scale), which hovers near zero or slightly negative (around -10 to 0) through most of 2020 and 2021, then becomes increasingly negative through 2022 and 2023, with the bars extending further downward toward the end of the series, reaching approximately -100 to -130 in late 2023.
